[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines the minimum validation rigor and quality thresholds required to move AI agents through lifecycle states and maintain acceptable output quality in production. It establishes the required validation assets, minimum quality dimensions, lifecycle quality gates, and defect management requirements that apply to all enterprise AI agents.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all lifecycle transitions and all productionized AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents. It governs the validation process, not the content of specific test scenarios — those are defined per capability in the quality rubric required by STD-TEC-AI-001.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. All lifecycle promotion decisions must comply with the quality gates defined in this standard.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Non-deterministic AI outputs require explicit validation rigor that does not exist in traditional software quality assurance. Without defined quality gates and defect management requirements, agents with unacceptable output quality or policy compliance issues may reach Production state and operate without remediation.

page_texts.9:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Required Validation Assets:**

Every agent must maintain the following validation assets before Pilot promotion, and keep them current throughout the Production lifecycle:

1. Scenario-based test suite — a set of representative input scenarios that cover the agent's in-scope intents and key edge cases
2. Expected-output criteria by scenario — for each test scenario, the criteria by which the output will be evaluated as passing or failing
3. Quality rubric with scoring thresholds — the quality dimensions and minimum acceptable scores per dimension
4. Defect taxonomy — the classification scheme for categorizing defects by type and severity
5. Regression baseline set — a documented set of scenarios that must continue to pass whenever a change is made to the agent

**Minimum Quality Dimensions:**

Every capability must be scored on all six dimensions in the quality rubric:

1. Completeness — all required sections and fields are present in the output
2. Accuracy — facts and extracted data in the output are correct against the source evidence
3. Relevance — the output addresses the intent and does not include irrelevant content
4. Prioritization quality — items are ordered or weighted correctly per the use case's decision context
5. Policy compliance — no prohibited content patterns are present; provenance and taxonomy requirements are met
6. Explainability or provenance quality — conclusions are traceable to evidence categories as required by STD-TEC-AI-003

**Lifecycle Validation Gates:**

_Proposed to Pilot:_
- All required deliverables from STD-TEC-AI-001 are complete
- Baseline scenario suite exists and passes the minimum threshold defined in the quality rubric
- High-Tech governance review confirms contract completeness

_Pilot to Production:_
- Production-grade scenario suite has passed all six quality dimension thresholds
- Defect rate is below the target defined in the quality rubric
- Rework rate is within the target defined in the quality rubric
- High-Tech governance review sign-off recorded

_Production maintenance:_
- Periodic regression checks per the agent's review cadence
- Quality trend monitoring; containment triggered when quality falls below threshold

**Defect Management Requirements:**

- Defects must be categorized by severity (informational, minor, major, critical) and root cause (accuracy, completeness, relevance, prioritization quality, policy compliance, schema, provenance)
- Repeat defects of the same root cause trigger a design-level remediation review, not just a prompt fix
- High-severity policy compliance defects trigger immediate containment regardless of overall quality score
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Design test scenarios that cover degraded-evidence conditions (per STD-TEC-AI-002) as well as full-evidence conditions
- Include scenarios that probe the out-of-scope boundaries defined in the capability contract — the agent should handle out-of-scope inputs gracefully without producing misleading outputs
- Record quality rubric scores after each scenario run to enable trend analysis over time
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Agents must not be promoted to Pilot without a completed scenario-based test suite and quality rubric
- Agents must not be promoted to Production without passing all six quality dimension thresholds
- Quality rubric scoring thresholds must not be reduced after the fact to pass a failing agent; threshold changes require architecture board approval
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Requests to override a lifecycle quality gate require written architecture board approval with a documented risk acceptance
2. Risk acceptances for overriding Production promotion gates must include a remediation timeline for reaching threshold

page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#scenario-suite-coverage]

#### Scenario Suite Coverage

- The scenario suite must cover 100% of in-scope intents defined in the capability contract
- At minimum, each intent must have one passing scenario and one edge case or boundary scenario
- Degraded-evidence scenarios per STD-TEC-AI-002 must be included for all Required evidence sources
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#quality-rubric-thresholds]

#### Quality Rubric Thresholds

- Minimum acceptable thresholds for each quality dimension are defined in the capability's quality rubric, not in this standard — this standard requires that thresholds be defined, not what they must be
- Thresholds must be specific enough to produce a binary pass/fail determination for each scenario; subjective thresholds that cannot be consistently applied by different reviewers do not satisfy the requirement
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#regression-baseline-integrity]

#### Regression Baseline Integrity

- The regression baseline set must include all scenarios that passed validation at the most recent lifecycle promotion
- Regression baseline scenarios must not be removed from the set without architecture board approval; scenarios may be added without approval

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#phase-1-validation-asset-authoring-before-pilot]

#### Phase 1: Validation Asset Authoring (Before Pilot)

1. Enumerate in-scope intents and draft test scenarios for each
2. Define expected-output criteria for each scenario against the output contract (STD-TEC-AI-003)
3. Define the quality rubric with scoring thresholds for all six quality dimensions
4. Define the defect taxonomy with severity levels and root cause categories
5. Run the baseline scenario suite and record results; confirm minimum threshold is met
page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#phase-2-production-validation-before-production-promotion]

#### Phase 2: Production Validation (Before Production Promotion)

1. Expand the scenario suite to production-grade coverage
2. Run all scenarios and score against the quality rubric
3. Confirm defect rate and rework rate are within targets
4. Submit quality scorecard to High-Tech governance reviewer
page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#phase-3-production-quality-maintenance]

#### Phase 3: Production Quality Maintenance

1. Run regression baseline set after each change to the agent
2. Sample agent outputs monthly and score against the quality rubric per STD-TEC-AI-003
3. Report quality trend in the monthly domain scorecard
page_texts.23:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Validation asset completeness | All 5 required validation assets present and substantive | Asset review during governance gate | Validation asset documents |
| Quality dimension coverage | All 6 quality dimensions have defined thresholds in the rubric | Rubric review | Quality rubric document |
| Lifecycle gate compliance | Agent has passed all required gates before each lifecycle promotion | Governance sign-off record | Governance review records |
| Defect categorization | All identified defects are categorized by severity and root cause | Defect log review | Defect log |

page_texts.25:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Missing validation assets: block lifecycle progression
- Sub-threshold quality scores: contain or require remediation before promotion
- Repeated severe defects (same root cause appearing in multiple review cycles): mandatory architecture board review
page_texts.26:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-005-ai-agent-quality-validation.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Platform Governance Team (quality gate process); High-Tech role leads (quality gate review)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (threshold override approvals; repeated severe defect escalation)
